chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Stuff's enlarged band and the sad fate of trumpeter Sleepy Tomlin
summary: Back in Buffalo the band had Dick Vance and St. Louis trumpeter William 'Sleepy' Tomlin, whose daughter was murdered in St. Louis and who then lost his mind.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Went on back there, and Stuff got -- enlarged the band some more.
Had Stuff put anybody in your place?
No. He had nobody in there, but there was another trumpet player already there when I left. I can't think who he was. Anyhow, we had Dick Vance and myself.
Yeah, and a guy named Sleepy, out of St. Louis. William Tomlin was his name. Good trumpet player. Different style from anybody I ever heard.
Well, he went back to St. Louis and somebody raped his daughter and put her in an ashcan, and he never got straight no more. He was --
Then he went crazy and died.
Oh, what a horrible story. Killed the little girl?
